Difference: "Electronics" vs "Electronic". This is spelling/morphological drift of the same company name. Also punctuation drift ("Co. LTD" vs "Co., LTD"). These are same-entity per the rules. Best value: which one? The rules say same-entity verdicts don't specify best_value explicitly except for number/year format (register's canonical form). For same-entity name drift, the fused record should carry... the rules only explicitly say document-noise → register value, different-entity → document value, number/year → register canonical. For same-entity spelling drift, we need to pick. The certificate is the legal instrument; document is likely authoritative for the name. But the register here is the OIML-CS database. Hmm.

Rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." No best_value specified for that case explicitly. I'll choose the document's value since certificate is the legal instrument (consistent with the different-entity rationale). Actually, one could argue register canonical. But the certificate document is the legal instrument; the name as printed on the certificate should be the fused value. I'll go with document value "Zhongshan Camry Electronic Co., LTD".

Verdict: same-entity. Why: only pluralization/punctuation drift of the same company name.
